question: In 2018, Ganesh and Kumaresh Rajagopalan won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Carnatic instrumental music. For playing which instrument did they win this award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Violin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The brothers Ganesh and Kumaresh Rajagopalan are celebrated violinists who won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2018) for Carnatic instrumental music on the violin. (वायलिन वादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The violin, though of Western origin, was adapted into Carnatic music and is played seated, held between the shoulder and the ankle.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, established in 1952.

NOTE

• Famous Carnatic violinists include Lalgudi Jayaraman, M. S. Gopalakrishnan and T. N. Krishnan.

question: Which of the following diseases is detected by the Widal test?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Typhoid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Widal test" is a serological test used to diagnose typhoid fever, caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi. (टाइफाइड — विडाल परीक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water; symptoms include high fever, weakness and abdominal pain.

• The Widal test detects antibodies (agglutinins) against Salmonella antigens (O and H).

NOTE

• Some diagnostic tests: ELISA/Western blot (HIV), Mantoux test (tuberculosis), RT-PCR (viral infections like COVID-19), Widal test (typhoid).

question: In which language was 'Mudraraksha' play written by Vishakhadatta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanskrit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mudrarakshasa" (Mudraraksha), the famous political drama by Vishakhadatta, was written in Sanskrit. It deals with the rise of Chandragupta Maurya and the strategies of Chanakya (Kautilya) against Rakshasa, the minister of the Nandas. (संस्कृत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Vishakhadatta also wrote Devichandraguptam.

• Mudrarakshasa is an important source for the history of the Maurya dynasty.

NOTE

• Other great Sanskrit dramatists: Kalidasa (Abhijnanashakuntalam), Bhasa (Swapnavasavadatta), Shudraka (Mrichchhakatika).

question: What does M stand for in BHIM-UPI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Money.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "BHIM" stands for "Bharat Interface for Money". So "M" stands for "Money". (भारत इंटरफ़ेस फ़ॉर मनी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• BHIM is a mobile payment app launched by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in December 2016, named after Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (Bhimrao).

• UPI stands for "Unified Payments Interface", a real-time inter-bank money transfer system.

NOTE

• UPI, developed by NPCI, allows instant fund transfers using a Virtual Payment Address (VPA) or QR code without sharing bank details.

question: As per Census 2011, what is the literacy rate of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 74.04%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, the overall literacy rate of India was 74.04%. (साक्षरता दर — 74.04%)

◦ Male literacy: about 82.14%; Female literacy: about 65.46%.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kerala was the most literate state (93.91%), and Bihar the least literate.

• A person aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language is counted as literate.

NOTE

• The Census 2011 was the 15th national census; Lakshadweep and Mizoram were among the most literate UT/states after Kerala.

question: Constipation could be a sign that the person in suffering from a lack of ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dietary Fibre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Constipation is commonly caused by a lack of dietary fibre (roughage) in the diet. Fibre adds bulk to stool and helps it move smoothly through the intestines. (आहार रेशा / फाइबर की कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dietary fibre is found in whole grains, fruits, vegetables and pulses; it is not digested but aids bowel movement and digestive health.

• Drinking enough water along with fibre helps prevent constipation.

NOTE

• Fibre is of two types: soluble (oats, fruits) and insoluble (whole grains, vegetable skins). Insoluble fibre especially helps prevent constipation.

question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution are borrowed from which country's constitution?
option_1: The Constitution of the United States
option_3: The Constitution of the United Kingdom
option_4: The Constitution of the Soviet Union
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Constitution of Ireland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland (which itself took the idea from Spain). (आयरलैंड — नीति निदेशक तत्व)

◦ DPSPs are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Borrowed features: Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review (USA); Parliamentary system, Rule of Law (UK); Fundamental Duties, Five-Year Plans (USSR); DPSP (Ireland).

• DPSPs are non-justiciable (not enforceable in courts) but fundamental in the governance of the country.

NOTE

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called the DPSPs "novel features" of the Constitution and the "conscience" guiding the State towards a welfare state.

question: In which of the following years did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1905.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy of India, announced the Partition of Bengal in 1905 (it came into effect on 16 October 1905). (बंगाल विभाजन — 1905)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The partition, officially for administrative convenience, was seen as a "divide and rule" move to weaken the nationalist movement by splitting Hindus and Muslims.

• It triggered the Swadeshi and Boycott Movements.

• The partition was finally annulled/reversed in 1911.

NOTE

• Lord Curzon (Viceroy 1899–1905) also passed the Indian Universities Act (1904) and set up the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in its modern form.

question: Which of the following is NOT a qualification/eligibility to become the President of India?
option_1: Must be a citizen of India
option_2: Must be qualified for election as a member of the house of the people
option_3: Must have completed the age of thirty-five years
option_4: Must hold any office of profit
solution_text:
The correct answer is Must hold any office of profit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Must hold any office of profit" is NOT a qualification — in fact, a candidate must NOT hold any office of profit under the Government to be eligible for President. (लाभ का पद धारण न करना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• As per Article 58, to be President a person must:

◦ be a citizen of India,

◦ have completed 35 years of age, and

◦ be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha (House of the People).

• The President is elected by an electoral college through the system of proportional representation by single transferable vote.

NOTE

• The President can hold an office of profit only if it is that of President, Vice-President, Governor, or a Minister of the Union or a State (these are not treated as disqualifying offices).

question: Losoong festival is predominantly celebrated in Sikkim by which of the following tribes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhutia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Losoong" (also called Namsoong) is a harvest/New Year festival celebrated in Sikkim, predominantly by the Bhutia community, marking the end of the harvest season. (लोसूंग — भूटिया जनजाति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Losoong is marked by traditional Chaam (masked) dances performed in monasteries.

• The Lepchas call it Namsoong; the festival usually falls in December.

NOTE

• Major tribes of Sikkim: Lepcha (original inhabitants), Bhutia and Nepali. The Bhil are of central/western India; the Khasi of Meghalaya; the Kurumba of the Nilgiris.

question: Which is the largest agro-based Industry of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cotton textile industry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Cotton textile industry" is the largest agro-based industry in India. It uses cotton (an agricultural product) as raw material and provides large-scale employment. (सूती वस्त्र उद्योग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first modern cotton mill was set up in Mumbai (1854).

• Major centres: Mumbai, Ahmedabad ("Manchester of India"), Coimbatore, Kanpur.

• The textile industry is one of the largest sources of employment after agriculture.

NOTE

• "Agro-based industries" use agricultural raw materials — e.g., cotton textiles, jute, sugar, tea, coffee, vegetable oil and paper industries.

question: Which of the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate finally annexed Jaunpur into the empire of Delhi Sultanate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lodi dynasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Lodi dynasty, specifically Bahlul Lodi, finally annexed the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur into the Delhi Sultanate (around 1479–1484). (लोदी वंश — जौनपुर का विलय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jaunpur was ruled by the independent Sharqi dynasty, famous for its architecture (e.g., Atala Masjid) and patronage of learning ("Shiraz of the East").

• The Lodi dynasty (1451–1526) was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate; Ibrahim Lodi was defeated by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

NOTE

• The five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate: Slave (Mamluk), Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi. The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty.

question: The property by virtue of which carbon can form a C-C covalent bond is called _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is catenation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Catenation" is the property by which carbon atoms link with one another to form long chains, branched chains and rings through C–C covalent bonds. (श्रृंखलन / कैटेनेशन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Carbon shows the maximum catenation because of its small size and strong C–C bonds.

• This property, along with tetravalency, is the reason for the huge number of organic compounds.

NOTE

• Allotropy = existence of an element in different physical forms (e.g., diamond, graphite, fullerene for carbon).

• Tetravalency = carbon's valency of four (it forms four bonds).

question: ________ received Padma Shri 2017 award for being an exponent of Nagpuri folk dance Jhumar.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mukund Nayak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mukund Nayak of Jharkhand received the Padma Shri (2017) for his contribution as an exponent of the Nagpuri folk dance and music, Jhumar. (मुकुंद नायक — झूमर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Jhumar is a popular folk song-and-dance tradition of the Nagpuri (Chhotanagpur) region of Jharkhand.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India, given for distinguished contribution in various fields.

NOTE

• Order of Padma awards: Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. Above them is the Bharat Ratna, the highest civilian award.

question: Who wrote the novel 'The Catcher in the Rye'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is JD Salinger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The novel "The Catcher in the Rye" (1951) was written by the American author J. D. Salinger. Its protagonist is the teenage rebel Holden Caulfield. (जे.डी. सैलिंजर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• H. G. Wells — *The Time Machine*, *The War of the Worlds*.

• Ernest Hemingway — *The Old Man and the Sea*, *A Farewell to Arms*.

• Mark Twain — *The Adventures of Tom Sawyer*, *Adventures of Huckleberry Finn*.

NOTE

• *The Catcher in the Rye* is a classic coming-of-age novel exploring teenage alienation and rebellion, widely studied in English literature.

question: Which of the following events and their hosts is correctly matched?
option_1: ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2011 – Australia and New Zealand
option_2: ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2015 – India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh
option_3: ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2019 – England and Wales
option_4: ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2007 – England
solution_text:
The correct answer is ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2019 – England and Wales.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2019 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup was correctly hosted by England and Wales, and won by England. (2019 विश्व कप — इंग्लैंड और वेल्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Correct host details:

◦ 2011 — India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (won by India).

◦ 2015 — Australia and New Zealand (won by Australia).

◦ 2007 — West Indies (won by Australia).

• Options 1, 2 and 4 have interchanged/incorrect hosts.

NOTE

• India won the 50-over World Cup in 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (M. S. Dhoni). Australia has won the most titles.

question: The Panchpatmali mineral deposit region is located in which state from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Panchpatmali" deposits (of bauxite, the ore of aluminium) are located in the Koraput district of Odisha. (पंचपटमाली — ओडिशा, बॉक्साइट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Panchpatmali is one of India's largest bauxite deposits and is mined by NALCO (National Aluminium Company).

• Odisha is the leading producer of bauxite in India.

NOTE

• Bauxite is the chief ore of aluminium. Other bauxite-rich states: Gujarat, Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh.

question: In 2023, the Government of India has proposed to set up how many new 'Waste to Wealth' plants under GOBARdhan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 500.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2023-24, the Government proposed setting up 500 new 'Waste to Wealth' plants under the GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) scheme. (गोबरधन — 500 संयंत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• These plants include compressed biogas (CBG) plants and aim to promote a circular economy.

• The GOBARdhan scheme converts cattle dung and organic waste into biogas and bio-fertiliser.

NOTE

• The 500 plants comprise 200 compressed biogas (CBG) plants (including 75 in urban areas) and 300 community/cluster-based plants, with an investment of about ₹10,000 crore.

question: Tirot Sing was the leader of which of the following revolts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khasi uprising.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tirot Sing (U Tirot Sing) was a Khasi chief who led the Khasi uprising (rebellion) against the British in the 1829–1833 period, in present-day Meghalaya. (तिरोत सिंह — खासी विद्रोह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The revolt began when the British tried to build a road through the Khasi Hills connecting Assam with Sylhet.

• Tirot Sing is remembered as a freedom fighter and folk hero of Meghalaya.

NOTE

• Other tribal revolts: Santhal Rebellion (1855–56), Munda Rebellion/Ulgulan (Birsa Munda), Kol Uprising, Sanyasi Revolt (Bengal).

question: To which state does the Indian tennis player Sumit Nagal belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian tennis player Sumit Nagal belongs to the state of Haryana (born in Jhajjar district). (सुमित नागल — हरियाणा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sumit Nagal won a junior Wimbledon doubles title (2015).

• He gained fame for winning a set against Roger Federer at the 2019 US Open and has represented India in the Davis Cup and Olympics.

NOTE

• Other notable Indian tennis players: Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Rohan Bopanna, Sania Mirza and Ramanathan Krishnan.

question: Which Indian Member of Parliament was given the 'India UK Outstanding Achievers Honour' in January 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raghav Chadha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Raghav Chadha, the Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha MP, was given the "India UK Outstanding Achievers Honour" in January 2023 (in London). (राघव चड्ढा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The honour recognises outstanding Indian achievers connected with the UK.

• Raghav Chadha is one of the youngest members of the Rajya Sabha, representing Punjab.

NOTE

• The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the permanent upper house of Parliament; the minimum age to become its member is 30 years.

question: ___________ dance is embedded in the stories from the epics Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kathakali", the classical dance-drama of Kerala, is based on stories drawn from the epics Mahabharata, Ramayana and the Puranas. It is known for its elaborate costumes, colourful face make-up and expressive gestures. (कथकली — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The word "Kathakali" comes from "katha" (story) and "kali" (play/performance).

• Male performers traditionally play all roles; the make-up colours (e.g., green for noble heroes) signify character types.

NOTE

• Eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: The Dravidian style of temple architecture can be largely seen from which part of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Southern India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Dravidian style" of temple architecture is largely seen in Southern India (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, etc.). (द्रविड़ शैली — दक्षिण भारत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Key features of the Dravidian style: a stepped pyramidal tower called the vimana, a gateway tower called the gopuram, and an enclosed temple complex with high compound walls.

• Examples: Brihadeeswara Temple (Thanjavur), Meenakshi Temple (Madurai), Shore Temple (Mahabalipuram).

NOTE

• The three main temple styles: Nagara (North India), Dravida (South India), and Vesara (Deccan — a hybrid style).

question: In India, who introduced the idea of the poverty line for the first time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dadabhai Naoroji was the first to introduce the idea of a poverty line in India, in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India". He also propounded the famous "Drain of Wealth" theory. (दादाभाई नौरोजी — निर्धनता रेखा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dadabhai Naoroji is known as the "Grand Old Man of India" and was the first Indian to become a British MP (in the House of Commons).

• He was thrice elected President of the Indian National Congress.

NOTE

• The "Drain of Wealth" theory argued that Britain was continuously draining India's wealth and resources, causing widespread poverty.

question: Layers of varying thickness are found in which type of rock?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedimentary rock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sedimentary rocks" are formed by the deposition and compaction of sediments in layers (strata) over long periods, so they show layers/beds of varying thickness. (अवसादी चट्टानें — परतदार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Examples of sedimentary rocks: sandstone, limestone, shale and coal.

• Sedimentary rocks are the main source of fossils, as remains of organisms get buried within their layers.

NOTE

• The three main rock types: Igneous (formed from cooled magma/lava), Sedimentary (formed in layers from sediments), and Metamorphic (formed by heat/pressure altering existing rocks).
